title: Threads, ownership and deterministic reductions
outcome: Run independent chunks on the prepared two-thread runtime, combine results deterministically and protect shared state with an explicit lock.

exercises.title: Derive the reduction oracle
exercises.task: Compute the sum of squares through 100 from the closed-form formula.
exercises.answer: The independent formula checks the reduction without copying its loop.

exercises.title: Trace an empty chunk
exercises.task: Explain how the single-element input handles its second range.
exercises.answer: The additive identity makes the empty partial result well-defined.

exercises.title: Explain lost updates
exercises.task: Trace two unprotected increments that read the same value.
exercises.expected: One update can overwrite the other.
exercises.hint: An increment is not one abstract atomic step.
exercises.answer: Locking the full read-modify-write operation prevents this schedule under the stated protocol.

exercises.title: Review scratch ownership
exercises.task: Explain why threadid-indexed buffers can be unsafe.
exercises.hint: A thread ID is not permanent task ownership.
exercises.answer: Task-owned state or explicit synchronization is safer than undocumented schedule assumptions.

exercises.title: Analyze floating reduction
exercises.task: Explain why changing grouping can change floating results.
exercises.hint: Associativity holds for real arithmetic, not all machine arithmetic.
exercises.answer: Use a justified tolerance or a numerically stable reduction when extending the integer example.

exercises.title: Design a performance comparison
exercises.task: State the boundaries needed to claim a parallel speedup.
exercises.expected: Include scheduling, work, reduction and thread configuration.
exercises.answer: Measure the full warmed operation with identical correct outputs and representative data.
